bib.title: Extending Context Window of Large Language Models via Positional Interpolation

legacy_report:
SOURCE: "Extending Context Window of Large Language Models via Position Interpolation", Shouyuan Chen, Sherman Wong, Liangjian Chen, Yuandong Tian (Meta Platforms Inc.). arXiv:2306.15595v2 [cs.CL], 28 Jun 2023. It is a preprint, and the text names no venue.

COVERAGE: All 18 pages. I read about 44,000 of 51,623 chars: the body, tables, appendices A to C, and the first part of the references. I skimmed the middle of the reference list and the end of the C.2 code (not read) for origins only. The extraction is clean.

CLAIMS (ranked)

- Claim: Directly extrapolating a RoPE model past its trained window fails catastrophically. Perplexity goes above 1000, comparable to an untrained model.
  number: >10^3 perplexity
  setup: LLaMA 7B, trained at 2048, evaluated at 4096 to 32768 on PG19 (Table 1).
  quote: "when directly extending to larger context windows unseen in the training, the perplexity may shoot up to very high numbers (i.e., > 103), comparable to untrained models."
  where: p.3, Sec 2.2; Table 1, p.7

- Claim: Position Interpolation (PI) rescales position indices from [0, L') to [0, L) before RoPE. It adds no weights and changes no architecture.
  number: f'(x,m) = f(x, mL/L')
  setup: RoPE models (LLaMA). Example in Fig 1: 4096 mapped down to 2048.
  quote: "instead of extrapolation, we directly down-scale the position indices so that the maximum position index matches the previous context window limit in the pre-training stage."
  where: p.2, Sec 1; Eq. 4, p.4

- Claim: PI needs very little fine-tuning. 1000 steps on the Pile is the default. The effective window reaches its target after about 200 steps.
  number: 1000 steps (200 steps for the effective window)
  setup: LLaMA 7B/33B, windows 8192, 16384, 32768. Passkey retrieval, kmax defined as the largest k where every k' ≤ k has at least 20% success.
  quote: "the effective context window size reaching maximum kmax = L′, after merely fine-tuning for 200 steps, consistently across both 7B and 33B model sizes and up to 32768 context windows."
  where: p.9, Sec 3.3; Table 4

- Claim: Direct fine-tuning to a longer window barely helps. After more than 10000 steps the effective window grew from 2048 to only 2560.
  number: 2048 to 2560 after 10000 steps
  setup: LLaMA 7B, 8192 target, no PI (Table 4).
  quote: "LLaMA models that are extended via direct fine-tuning only saw a minimal increase of the effective context window size kmax from 2048 to 2560, even after fine-tuning for more than 10000 steps"
  where: p.9; p.1

- Claim: Without any fine-tuning, PI already gives a usable model at 8192. Fine-tuning then improves it quickly.
  number: 16.10 at 8192 (step 0), 7.12 at step 200, 6.95 at step 1000. For 16384: 112.13 at step 0, then 7.05 and 6.83.
  setup: LLaMA 7B, PG19 perplexity (Table 3). Original 2048 model scores 7.20 at 2048.
  quote: "7B 8192 16.10 7.12 7.10 7.02 6.99 6.95" and "At 200 steps the models surpassed the original model's perplexity on 2048 context window size"
  where: p.7-8, Table 3

- Claim: Perplexity falls steadily as the window grows under PI. Direct fine-tuning (FT) regresses as the window grows.
  number: PG19, 7B at 32768 window: 7.23 (at 2048), 7.04, 6.91, 6.80, 6.77 (at 32768). 7B FT at 8192: 7.21, 7.34, 7.69.
  setup: PG19 test (100 docs), sliding window stride 256. Proof-pile is a 128-doc subsample truncated to 32768 tokens.
  quote: "7B 32768 PI 7.23 7.04 6.91 6.80 6.77" ; "models extended via the direct fine-tuning method has shown regression (up to +0.48) or minor improvement (up to -0.12)"
  where: p.6-7, Table 1 and Table 2

- Claim: PI costs a little at short context. Proof-pile perplexity at 2048 degrades by 0.01 to 0.05. Zero-shot benchmark drops reach up to 2% at 8192, and more at longer extensions.
  number: 0.01 to 0.05 perplexity; up to 2%. 7B BoolQ falls from 76.1 to 73.2 (8192), 69.8 (16384), 64.7 (32768).
  setup: LLaMA 7B and 33B, benchmarks within 2048 tokens (Table 5).
  quote: "with a degradation of up to 2% on the benchmark tasks, for both 7B and 33B model sizes. Models extended to longer context windows regressed more on the benchmarks"
  where: p.6-7, p.9; Table 5, p.10

- Claim: Interpolation error is bounded far below extrapolation error.
  number: ~600x smaller
  setup: Theoretical, LLaMA 7B (d=128, c=10000). Interpolation bound is d·max|hj|/294.73. The extrapolation bound is at least 2× larger than that bound's coefficient.
  quote: "the interpolation bound is at least 2 · 294.73 ∼ 600× smaller than the extrapolation bound"
  where: p.5, Sec 2.3; Eq 7-8; proof in App. A

- Claim: Extrapolated attention scores can blow up outside the trained range, even though they stay near ±1 inside it.
  number: values above 8000
  setup: Least-squares fit of Eqn 3 with d=128, L=2048, random points. Illustrative, not the trained model.
  quote: "out of this region it may goes beyond 8000, causing catastrophic issues in attention computation."
  where: p.4, Fig 2 caption

- Claim: Summarisation at a 16K window is competitive but not best.
  number: ROUGE-1/2/L 60.0 / 28.0 / 29.5
  setup: GovReport, inputs truncated to the first 15000 tokens, PI-16384 LLaMA-7B fine-tuned 10 epochs. CoLT5 XL 16K scores 61.3 / 32.2 / 33.8.
  quote: "LLaMA-7B Extended 16K 60.0 28.0 29.5"
  where: p.9-10, Table 6

- Claim: Context extension runs up to 32× on the same recipe. Training used 128 A100s for most cases and 32 A100s for 7B/13B/33B at 8192.
  number: 32×, 32768 from 2048
  setup: Learning rate 2e-5 for 7B/13B and 1e-5 for 33B/65B. Batch 64 or 128. AdamW, 20-step warmup.
  quote: "We show Position Interpolation can effectively extend context window up to 32 times of the original size"
  where: p.6, Sec 3 and 3.1

- Claim: Perplexity gain from longer context is modest. 2048 to 16384 gives -0.28 (PG19) and -0.5 (proof-pile) for 7B. 65B at 8192 gains -0.12 and -0.3.
  number: -0.28 / -0.5 (7B), -0.27 / -0.48 (13B), -0.14 / -0.42 (33B), -0.12 / -0.3 (65B)
  setup: 65B is extended only to 8192.
  quote: "we observed -0.28 and -0.5 reductions of perplexity for extending LLaMA 7B models on both datasets"
  where: p.6

LIMITS
- The method applies to RoPE models. Learnable absolute embeddings such as OPT are only conjectured to work, and "we plan to investigate this in the future".
- The paper reports mild degradation within the original window, and says a small degradation "is expected since Position Interpolation forces position encodings in original context window to reside in a much narrower region".
- The passkey task is synthetic. It uses a 5-digit key, 10 trials at each of 32 positions, and a 20% success threshold. Passing it does not show quality at long range, and the paper has no multi-hop or reasoning long-context evaluation.
- The 7B 32768 model's proof-pile perplexity rises at the longest window (2.24 at 16384 to 2.48 at 32768). The paper does not discuss this. Table 4 also has an odd 18432 entry for 7B 32768 at 600 steps.
- Inference cost: full attention over all tokens costs more ("albeit with higher inference costs"). Memory and attention cost are not measured.
- 65B is evaluated only at 8192. Summarisation is shown for one model and one dataset.
- The theory bounds attention score, not task quality. The PI bound compares against the RoPE paper's extrapolation bound, which the authors call loose.
- It has dated. Later methods (NTK-aware scaling, YaRN, etc.) are not covered. I know that from outside the text, not from the paper.

BUILDS ON
- RoPE: Su et al., 2021 (RoFormer), the position encoding used in LLaMA (Touvron et al., 2023).
- Position-embedding interpolation: Dosovitskiy et al., 2021 (Vision Transformer). It interpolated learned embeddings up to 4×. PI interpolates indices instead.
- Concurrent work: kaiokendev (2023, SuperHOT blog), Reddit and llama.cpp discussions, and LoRA (Hu et al., 2021).
- Length extrapolation: ALiBi (Press et al., 2022), LeX (Sun et al., 2022), Haviv et al., 2022.
- Passkey task: Mohtashami & Jaggi, 2023. Sliding-window perplexity: Press et al., 2022.
- Data: Pile (Gao et al., 2020), PG-19 (Rae et al., 2020), proof-pile, RedPajama, GovReport (Huang et al., 2021), SCROLLS.
- Hypothesis it reaffirms: Vaswani et al., 2017.
- Compared with or complementary to: CoLT5 (Ainslie et al., 2023), retrieval-augmented LLMs, landmark attention, memory transformers.

CODE
- p.4, Eq. 4: `f'(x, m) = f(x, m·L/L')`. This is the whole method.
- App. C.1 (p.17) fits sin/cos bases by least squares on positions 0 to 2047 and evaluates over 0 to 4095 to show the extrapolation blow-up. It is a demonstration, not the method.

FIGURES (captions read from the extraction, no figure tool run)
- Fig 1 (p.2): Position Interpolation versus extrapolation. It shows position indices 0 to 4096 squashed into the 0 to 2048 range. It is the fastest way to see the method.
- Fig 2 (p.4): fitted attention score. It is bounded within [0, 2048], above 8000 beyond 2048 (extrapolation), and smooth between integer positions (interpolation).
- Fig 3 (p.8): passkey prompt format.
- Fig 4 (p.10): summarisation prompt.
- Fig 5 (p.16): B(s)/d is at least 1.

PROBLEMS: None. The text contained no instructions to me. The tables extracted cleanly. Fig 2 and Fig 5 axes are garbled but their captions are readable. The author affiliation is Meta Platforms Inc.

For the target note `03-budgeting-the-window.md`: the claims most relevant to budgeting the window are that nominal window size, effective window (passkey kmax) and in-window quality are separate quantities, and that extension trades a small short-context loss for long-range use. This is my inference from the claims above, not something the paper says. I did not open the note.
